correctness.rationale: Set u=Ab, w=b, alpha=u·w/||u||^2>0 and delta^2=||w||^2/||u||^2-alpha^2. With Gaussian sketch S independent of fixed b, orthogonal Gaussian components g,h yield R=Theta^(-1)=alpha+delta(g·h)/||g||^2 distributed as alpha+(delta/sqrt(s))T_s. For delta>0 its Student density is smooth and positive at 0, hence Theta=1/R has both sign tails f_R(0)/t, absolute moment cutoff p<1, and no signed first moment. The characteristic function has expansion 1+i m_PV t -pi f_R(0)|t|+o(|t|), so iid arithmetic means converge to nondegenerate Cauchy(m_PV,pi f_R(0)). Independently checked 2D exact SPD example A=diag(1,2), b=(1,1), alpha=3/5, delta=1/5, s=1, f_R(0)=1/(2*pi). Eigenvector delta=0 gives constant exceptional case. This concerns fixed finite s, not simultaneous s,N limits.

value.rationale: The precise heavy-tail obstruction to averaging Gaussian-sketch harmonic Ritz values is a natural phenomenon in a broadly used numerical linear-algebra estimator. It distinguishes convergence under sufficient embedding events from unconditional finite-sketch moments and demonstrates that adding independent sketches without increasing sketch dimension cannot consistently average the harmonic estimator, despite the SPD underlying matrix.
